title: Alamut Castle
visualBrief: Roofless Alamut upper-castle ruins on a narrow fluted rock ridge, with ten mapped ruin groups, northwest cells, open rock-cut reservoirs, brick arch remnants, broken stone walls and eastern approach stairs.

nativeAxes.origin: Retained signed upper-castle anchor; Y0 decoded 2098.7457 m numeric working datum.

reconstruction.basis: OSM upper-castle outline and ruin groups; UNESCO 2024 aerial/ground photographs; published Willey ground plan and 2014 field photographs for cisterns and northwest ridge.
reconstruction.verticalDatum: Fresh exact-Q4706020 way 590499418 v3 and all retained component/stair/ruin coordinates match within 0.662 mm. Native +X points southeast at 135.629 degrees and +Z southwest at 225.629 degrees. Northwest cistern/cell ridge, southeast excavation/gate and approach plus Willey north arrow sign the direction. Retained public Terrarium numeric heights form a 16641-value 4 m native grid over a 512 m window. Y0 is decoded 2098.7457 m anchor working datum, not a surveyed regional/ellipsoidal datum. Architectural bodies receive one rigid -25.47 m shift; retained sloping plateau intercept becomes 12.53 m above anchor. This translation is constrained by retained terrain at ruin bases, cut-reservoir floors and interpreted incoming stair route with 0.25 m allowance. It is not an archaeological elevation survey. Local cliff shell and occupied ledge feet extend 4 m below sampled terrain; all five reservoir floors remain above the retained host ground. No whole-precinct terrain cutout/replacement. The host supplies the rest of the mountain.
reconstruction.state: Surviving roofless archaeological remains. Temporary excavation shelters in older photographs are omitted in the 2024 interpretation.

terrainReference.basis: Retained Terrarium grid center relative to decoded working anchor datum.

scaleBasis: Map outlines in meters; +X 45.63 degrees south of east. Only the horizontal outer envelope and mapped ruin footprints are georeferenced; heights and chamber subdivisions remain approximate.
geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
dataAttribution: Map geometry © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. UNESCO/ACHB photographs and published plan are references only; no pixels or third-party mesh copied.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.

Numeric Terrarium tile spacing and 4 m review grid do not establish native DEM resolution or vertical accuracy. Small rocky crest, caves and archaeological cuts are smoothed.
A rigid architectural translation is chosen to clear retained terrain at mapped ruin bases, cut-reservoir floors and the interpreted approach route. This is not a measured archaeological floor datum.
The retained sloping plateau and local cliff shell belong to this exterior reconstruction. Cliff bottoms extend below sampled host terrain, without including the full mountain.
All five cut-reservoir floors remain above retained host heights, avoiding a whole-precinct terrain cutout. Compatibility with other terrain vintages/products remains unverified.
Exact geological flutes, broken-wall profiles, reservoir depths and positions, cave passages and modern route elevations require a surveyed archaeological model.

Accepted exterior scope is mapped upper castle only. Lower/onion castle, passing zone and complete mountain are host terrain or outside this source coverage. Temporary excavation shelters/scaffolding are omitted from the 2024 interpretation. Interior caves and tunnel network are not supplied.

Six shared rubble masonry, weathered stone, brick, plaster, timber and painted-metal graphs. Bedrock and dark reservoir floors share tinted weathered stone; no embedded photographs or per-model bitmap copies. Regular sandstone masonry joints and floating relief chips are removed from bedrock and ruined walls. Exact geological ribs and archaeological floor details are simplified.
Broken walls, arch positions, subdivisions, reservoir depths and approach elevations are plan/photo interpretations, not measured archaeology. Physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
